Griffin: A Substrate node that supports Plutus by TxPipe - Milestone #1 Report

We are glad to announce the successful completion of Milestone #1 for the Griffin Catalyst project.

Evidence of milestone completion:
・Source-code available in our Github repository

https://github.com/txpipe/griffin/tree/catalyst-ms1
・Binary releases available in Github release section

https://github.com/txpipe/griffin/releases/tag/catalyst-ms1
・Video showcasing the basic node and idle operation

 https://drive.google.com/file/d/1gbjxbCLAG0jc3auyRgMCMraAVvX5dFV5/view

Milestone goals and proofs of completion
The list of features and requirements is available in our repository README. In this milestone, we have completed the following:
・The interface for the new Substrate runtime matches the feature requirements:
・RPC interface: a mechanism to interact with the node using a network RPC interface, used for extrinsic event submission and management operations.

You can check https://github.com/txpipe/griffin/blob/catalyst-ms1/node/src/rpc.rs for implementation details on the node side. This functionality is tested by use of the UTxO Wallet, which submits transactions via RPC requests.
・Aura consensus: a proof-of-authority (PoA) consensus protocol where only approved nodes are allowed to create new blocks.
・Grandpa block finality: a Byzantine fault tolerant finality gadget that provides deterministic finality.

Both features appear in the implementation of the relevant API traits of the Runtime. Presently, all Authority identities are hard-coded, but we have tested the node for inclusion of other ids by way of the command-line interface. The node counterpart of both is configured when a new client service is created.
・Libp2p networking: a battle-tested peer-to-peer networking library providing transport, discovery and routing mechanisms.

This is configured by use of Substrate’s sc_network crate, when a new service is built upon node initialization.

Milestone goals and proofs of completion

The list of features and requirements is available in our repository README. In this milestone, we have completed the following:
The implemented ledger resembles the Cardano ledger, with the exception of any staking, delegation or governance primitives.
The Transaction type defined in griffin-core has been cumulatively constructed by using primitives analogous to the ones in the Babbage era of Cardano (with outputs of the “post-Alonzo” style. An interface with the verification tools from Pallas was defined, which are then used by the Executive module to validate transactions. 
The implemented ledger contains the primitives required for UTxO programmability (datums, redeemers, scripts, etc).
This can be observed by visiting types.rs, where all those elements are defined. Namely, Datums are represented by a byte vector containing a CBOR. An example FakeDatum is used to showcase coding and decoding (at the wallet, for instance). 
PlutusScripts have an analogous format, and Redeemers for spending and minting are also provided.
Results from integration testing
We have successfully run two and three nodes simultaneously, allowing us to verify that the Aura and Grandpa consensus work as expected. The instructions to run two nodes with a single authoring one are detailed in our Readme.

ms.report:
Evidence of milestone completion

Milestone goals and proofs of completion

・The application is built using the Substrate framework and runs as a custom network.

As showcased in the video, we are interacting with our Griffin node (built with Substrate) through our wallet to build and submit transactions needed for creating, canceling and resolving orders from the Order Book dApp. Also, as explained in the README, the network can be extended to a custom number of synchronized nodes (this is a feature provided by the Substrate framework). 
・The application uses an UTxO-based ledger

All the dApp transactions are built using our off-chain code, in particular the pay_to_script and spend_script functions, that make use of the types defined in griffin-core, which are simplified versions from the Cardano ledger.
・The application relies on Plutus script for validation of some transactions

When creating an order, a control token must be minted. When canceling or resolving, a script input must be consumed and the control token must be burnt. In all those cases, Plutus scripts are run. If the conditions specified in the dApp aiken source code are not met, the transactions are rejected by the node with a phase two error.
